newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai PM says IMF thinks economy will recover by '99.
newsitem.headline: Thai PM says IMF thinks economy will recover by '99.

text.p: Thai prime minister Chavalit Yongchaiyudh said on Tuesday the International Monetary Fund (IMF) projects that the country's economy will recover by 1999.

"IMF projections showed that the Thai economy would be restored by the year 1999," Chavalit told reporters after a cabinet meeting which discussed a series of economic measures to help boost the country's economy.

Chavalit said Thailand needed about $15 billion in loans to help stabilise the economy. "There are many financial institutions offering loans and we estimate we need about $15 billion. The IMF said the economy would recover because the basic fundamentals are already strong," he said.
Chavalit also said the government was willing to cut up to 100 billion baht off the 1997/98 (October-September) budget which was set at 982 billion baht.
"If it's needed, the government is willing to cut the budget for the coming fiscal year by up to 100 billion baht," he said.

His comments came shortly after announcements by top financial authorities that Thailand would implement a series of tough measures in order to obtain between $12-$15 billion in loans from the IMF and foreign countries.
